title: When life expectancy was 28
hook: A newborn in late-1600s Breslau could expect about 28 years. What about a 30-year-old?

knows: life expectancy is "how long people live"
doesNotKnow: that life expectancy is an average from birth, so infant and child deaths pull it far below the age most adults reached

misconception: In the past, when life expectancy was about 30, people usually died around 30.
objective: The learner can explain that a low life expectancy at birth comes from many infant and child deaths, and that in Halley's Breslau table those who reached 30 died, on average, at about 58.

claims.text: Halley's table gives the people alive at each age, out of one year's births: 1,000 at 1, 732 at 5, 531 at 30, 346 at 50, 142 at 70, 41 at 80 (the stage draws every age from 0 to 84).
claims.source: history-data.mjs: halley, HalleyLifeTable.csv, column number (ages 1-84). Copied into Demo.tsx as SURVIVORS; history-cycle1-check.mjs section 1, 'survivors readout'.

claims.text: Halley took 1,238 births a year as the starting cohort ("of 1,238 born", age 0 on the chart).
claims.source: history-data.mjs: halley, HistData documentation for HalleyLifeTable (opened); Halley 1693 itself not opened. history-cycle1-check.mjs section 1 uses P[0] = 1238.

claims.text: The table is Halley's 1693 table for Breslau (question: "Halley's 1693 Breslau table"; hook: "late-1600s Breslau").
claims.source: history-data.mjs: halley (what: 'Halley's 1693 Breslau life table'), HistData documentation for HalleyLifeTable (opened). Primary: Halley, E. (1693), Phil. Trans. 17: 596-610, not opened. Breslau data years 1687-1691 per the Breslau doc (c6).

claims.text: From this table, life expectancy at birth is about 28 years; about 41% of those born died before age 5 (506 of 1,238); those alive at 30 died, on average, at about 58; those alive at 60 at about 72.
claims.source: history-cycle1-check.mjs section 1: e0 = 27.87 (trapezoid between whole ages), 30 + e30 = 57.7 (at most 58.3 if the 20 people alive at 84 lived 16 more years each), 60 + e60 = 72.1, died before 5 = 40.9%. Demo.tsx computes the same values live from SURVIVORS with the same trapezoid rule (avgDeath) and rounds to whole numbers.

claims.text: Life expectancy at birth averages over everyone born, infants included, so a low number does not mean adults died young; people who got through childhood usually lived much longer.
claims.source: Follows from c4: the average from birth (28) is below the average from 30 (58) because 41% of deaths came before age 5. Cross-check on separate records, not shown to the learner: Bellhouse's Breslau deaths 1687-91 give a mean age at death of 57.4 for those dying over 30 (history-data.mjs: breslau; history-cycle1-check.mjs section 1).

claims.text: Where it stops: this is one city's records over five years.
claims.source: history-data.mjs: breslau, HistData documentation for Breslau (data years 1687-1691, one city). Brief #1 lists no held source sentence in the reveal.

recall.question: A country's life expectancy at birth rises from 50 to 70, mostly because fewer babies die. Must adults now live 20 years longer?
options: No: most of the rise can come from infants surviving
recall.why: Life expectancy at birth averages over everyone born, so fewer infant deaths raise it even if adults live no longer than before.
